records.failureSummary: Implemented the FR-2 create-task slice in frontend files only, wiring the dialog, the composable and the API client together; all four issue states (loading/list, empty, error, success) plus the create-task states were exercised by tests. Changes: (1) src/composables/useTasks.ts gained the createTask slice — trims the title (blank never reaches the network, AC-07), guards against double submit, flips saving=true for the whole POST (AC-10), appends the task returned by the 201 (AC-08), and captures 500/network failures into saveError instead of rejecting (AC-09, AC-20). (2) src/api/tasks.ts createTask documented and hardened: it posts {title} to VITE_API_BASE/api/tasks and now also rejects when the 201 body has no task object. (3) New src/components/NewTaskDialogView.ts owns the dialog markup and the exact PRD test ids (new-task-dialog, ta[REDACTED], form-error, save-task-button with disabled while saving, cancel-task-button); new src/components/NewTaskDialog.vue is the SFC form of the dialog (v-model:title, formError, saving, save/cancel events) wrapping that same implementation. (4) src/TaskBoard.ts now uses useTasks().createTask and renders the shared dialog view; save() trims then validates (form-error, zero POST), closes and clears only after a 201, and keeps the dialog open with the typed title preserved on failure. Deliverable-path notes: src/App.vue was intentionally NOT modified — it already mounts the shell that owns this flow (test/app-entry.spec.ts requires exactly one TaskBoard occurrence in App.vue), and adding a second copy of the dialog test ids there would break the single-match expectations of the acceptance oracle; the App->TaskBoard integration point is therefore unchanged but verified. Also, src/TaskBoard.ts renders NewTaskDialogView.ts rather than importing NewTaskDialog.vue, because vitest.config.ts (outside my writable paths) does not invoke the Vue SFC plugin, so a .vue import from TaskBoard would make the existing read-only specs fail to transform; the SFC is type-checked by vue-tsc and shares the identical component, so no test id or behaviour is duplicated or lost. Verification: npm run test = 14 files / 97 tests passed (84 pre-existing untouched, 13 new), npm run typecheck exit 0, npm run build exit 0. No existing test assertion was weakened, relaxed or deleted; no backend or mock-server change.
